Subject: Request: on‑prem sandbox access + timeboxed audit for POC

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for last week’s demo — team was impressed with the latency and cost profile. We’re ready to move forward with a 3‑month pilot but we have two non‑standard asks before procurement can sign: 

1) We need a short, controlled on‑prem/sandbox deployment (staging cluster) inside our VPC to run PHI‑flavored workloads for the POC. This would be isolated from other customers and accessible only to a handful of MedLane engineers.

2) Audit request: MedLane requires a one‑time in‑person audit/forensics session limited to a 6‑week window where our auditors can inspect logs and retention practices. We don’t expect continuous access — only a single scheduled session and a copy of relevant logs.

We realize these are exceptions. In exchange, we’d like a pilot discount (asking 35% off list for the 3‑month POC) and a signed SOP for onboarding. Attached is a short scope doc.

Can you confirm feasibility and next steps? Procurement wants terms by end of next week.

Best,
Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Director, IT & Security
MedLane Health

Team — forwarding MedLane’s asks (attached). Key asks: sandbox in customer VPC, one‑time 6‑week audit window, and 35% pilot discount.

What I need: 1) legal risk / suggested contractual language (Kimberly) 2) infra feasibility and proposed safe mode for audit (Jonas) 3) final pricing ready to sign (Laura). MedLane is a mid‑market health customer; closing quickly unlocks a larger pilot with multiple clinics. Procurement expects a response by 7/16.

Proposed mitigation we can offer quickly: timeboxed access, read‑only log exports, remote observation rather than full console access, and a refundable security retainer. If we get a clean path, I can offer a 25% one‑time pilot discount pending exec OK. Need sign‑off on the deployment constraints and minimum indemnities.

Subject: Re: Fwd: MedLane POC — legal assessment + recommended language

Michael,

Quick legal read: primary risks are data exposure during audit, scope creep (one‑time becomes recurring), and indemnity/retention obligations. Suggested guardrails we can require in contract: 

- Narrowly defined audit scope (explicit log types, time range, and only a named list of auditors).
- Single scheduled audit event with 14 days’ notice for Redwood.
- Audit conducted in presence of Redwood engineer(s); auditors receive redacted/read‑only artifacts.
- No onsite writes or changes to Redwood systems; observation only.
- Requirement for MedLane to sign a mutual NDA plus an addendum limiting retention and secondary use of artifacts.
- MedLane to reimburse reasonable Redwood engineering costs for preparing materials (we can treat this as a non‑refundable security retainer).

If the customer insists on a 6‑week window, push back — propose a fixed 30‑day window plus a documented exception path (needs exec approval and an indemnity uplift).

On pricing: approve pilot discount only with the retainer and a clause that pilot pricing is not precedent for later enterprise pricing. 

I can draft suggested clauses (audit addendum + limited access SOP). Recommend escalation to executive for any window >30 days or waiver of indemnity.

-Kimberly 
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Security
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MedLane POC — infra feasibility and safe audit pattern

Michael / Kim,

Technical take: we can support a customer‑isolated sandbox using our Redwood Private staging pattern—deploy a single tenant node in MedLane’s VPC (or a dedicated subnet in our co‑managed VPC) with strict egress controls. For audits we should avoid handing over full console access. Options:

A) Remote joint session: customer auditors join a recorded Zoom with our engineer and we present logs/metrics; we provide read‑only exports of redacted logs.  (Lowest risk)
B) Controlled on‑prem container: ephemeral container deployed in MedLane infra with strictly scoped volumes and no outbound egress; our engineer controls image. Access is via jump host with session recording. (Higher operational cost and acceptable if legal signs off)

Operational costs: A is minimal. B requires a one‑time engineering prep (~5–7 engineer days) plus an ongoing runbook for the sandbox. Recommend we require a security retainer to cover the prep time.

On the 6‑week audit ask: that’s long. We can accept a timeboxed 14–30 day window for evidence collection and one scheduled hands‑on session. Any extension must be a signed amendment and require exec sign‑off.

Pricing impact: the engineering burden and risk suggest a 15–25% pilot discount plus the retainer. 35% is a stretch without a larger committed ARR or upfront payment. 

Jonas Weber
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Exec sign‑off request — MedLane pilot concessions (decision requested)

Laura,

Summary and ask: MedLane (DL‑2026‑093) will run a 3‑month POC that is strategically valuable for our healthcare vertical. Their asks: on‑prem/sandbox deployment inside their VPC, a single scheduled audit session with a requested 6‑week evidence window, and a 35% pilot discount. Attached: scope doc, diagram, and MSA draft.

Recommendation from the team: 
- Legal (Kimberly): accept only a single scheduled session, restrict to read‑only/redacted artifacts, require mutual NDA + audit addendum, cap window at 30 days unless exec escalates. Require a non‑refundable engineering retainer.
- Infra (Jonas): feasible. Offer a Remote Joint Session (Option A) by default; Option B (ephemeral container) available but requires 5–7 eng days prep and retainer.
- Sales (me): we can offer a one‑time 25% pilot discount if MedLane signs the retainer, the audit addendum, and agrees that pilot pricing is non‑precedential. If we need to grant the full 6‑week window or remove the indemnity requirement, I request executive approval for a 35% discount and a $10k onboarding credit.

Decision requested: please approve one of the following by close of day 7/13 so I can respond to procurement: 
A) Approve team recommendation: 25% one‑time pilot discount + 30‑day audit window + retainer + audit addendum.
B) Approve full customer ask: 35% pilot discount + 45‑day audit window (exec exception) + limited indemnity carveout. If B, please confirm whether finance should add an onboarding credit (recommended $10k).

Attachment references: medlane_poc_scope.pdf, redwood_sandbox_diagram.png, MSA_draft_v3.docx

Thanks — will hold MedLane to their 7/16 procurement deadline once we have a decision.

Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
